items.summary: Only the vanilla controllers move focus when a letter is typed; the React, Vue and Angular menus and trees ignore printable keys. One core helper, createTypeahead, serves Menu and TreeView in the four adapters and replaces the two inline vanilla buffers.

surface.core: New exports createTypeahead, isTypeaheadKey and the type Typeahead.

endState.behaviour: In an open Menu and in a TreeView, a key that is one character, not a space, pressed without Ctrl, Meta or Alt and not during composition, moves focus to the next entry after the focused one (wrapping, disabled entries skipped) whose normalised label starts with the typed buffer. The buffer clears 500 ms after the last key; repeating one letter cycles through the entries that start with it. preventDefault is called only when an entry was found, so an unmatched key keeps its default action. TreeView searches the visible (expanded) nodes only and works in a read-only tree (focus is not a value). The buffer is cleared when the menu closes and when the component is destroyed. Space and Enter keep their meaning (activate, select). Server rendering: the helper is created with the component, holds no DOM reference and starts its timer only inside next(), so no timer exists on the server.

core.signature: createTypeahead(options?: {timeout?: number}): Typeahead; interface Typeahead { next(key: string, labels: readonly string[], current: number, isDisabled?: (index: number) => boolean): number; reset(): void }
core.behaviour: New file core/src/typeahead.ts, exported from core/src/index.ts. next(): appends normalizeSearch(key) to the buffer (an empty normalised key returns -1 and leaves the buffer), restarts the timeout (default 500 ms) that clears the buffer, takes search = the single character when every character of the buffer is the same, else the buffer, then for offset 1..labels.length tests index (current + offset) mod length and returns the first index that is not disabled and whose normalizeSearch(label) starts with search; -1 when none. current = -1 starts at index 0. reset() clears buffer and timer. No DOM access, no global read at module evaluation.

core.signature: isTypeaheadKey(event: {key: string; ctrlKey?: boolean; metaKey?: boolean; altKey?: boolean}): boolean
core.behaviour: true when [...event.key].length === 1, event.key !== ' ' and none of ctrlKey, metaKey, altKey is set. Callers return before calling it while event.isComposing.

items.component: Menu (contract) and the packaged trigger of Menu and Popover
items.summary: The Menu differs in item shape, action name, open control, trigger text, trigger look and rendered structure. One item shape {value, label, disabled?, href?}, one action name, controlled and uncontrolled `open` in every framework, the documented vanilla markup as the DOM, and one trigger rule: the application's element in React, a packaged button named by `triggerLabel` with `triggerVariant` (default 'secondary') in Vue and Angular.

surface.react: Menu: `disabled?: boolean` (default false, new). `label` follows RootName: `MenuProps = MenuBaseProps & RootName`; an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` prop names the menu and is not written on the root. MenuItem unchanged: {value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; href?: string; onSelect?: () => void} (onSelect stays a React-only convenience). onAction(value), open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange unchanged. No triggerLabel and no triggerVariant: `trigger` is the application's element.

Popover: `triggerVariant?: ButtonVariant` (new, default 'secondary'); `triggerLabel` is declared without `required: true` and required unless the `trigger` slot is given. ButtonVariant is the union of Button's `variant` prop, exported from vue/src/forms.ts.

Exactly the active item has tabindex=0, the others -1. Trigger in Vue and Angular: button.hw-button[type=button][data-variant={triggerVariant}][aria-haspopup=menu][aria-expanded=true|false][aria-controls={menu id}][disabled when the menu is disabled] containing triggerLabel (Vue: the trigger slot instead when given). Popover trigger: the same button without aria-haspopup. Stated difference: in React the trigger is the application's element, to which the component adds aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls and, when the menu is disabled, disabled. The root div carries no aria-label. The controller hooks of the vanilla markup (data-hw-trigger, data-hw-panel, data-hw-value) are not rendered by the frameworks (conventionConflicts).
endState.behaviour: Trigger: click, Enter or Space toggles and focuses the first enabled item; ArrowDown opens on the first, ArrowUp on the last enabled item. Menu: ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Home / End move a roving focus over enabled items, type-ahead as in nav-b-1, Escape closes and focuses the trigger, Tab closes without moving focus, an outside press or focus leaving closes without moving focus. Activating an item notifies the action once with item.value, closes the menu and focuses the trigger; a link item then navigates natively; a disabled item is skipped by the keys and ignores a click. `open` follows convention controlled-and-observable-state: one notification per change, none when the application changes the controlled value, the DOM follows the application's value when controlled. When the application opens the menu, the first enabled item becomes the active one and is focused after the render, in the browser only. A disabled menu has a disabled trigger and is closed (an open one closes and notifies false once). Server rendering: closed unless `open` or `defaultOpen` (Angular: `open`) says otherwise; no focus call and no document listener on the server.

items.summary: Only the vanilla popover closes when focus moves out of it; in React, Vue and Angular tabbing past the panel leaves it open over later content. Every adapter closes a non-modal popup when focus moves to an element outside its root, without moving focus.

endState.behaviour: While open, a focusout whose relatedTarget is an element outside the component root (trigger and panel together) closes the popup, notifies open=false once and leaves focus on the element that received it. A focusout without a relatedTarget (the window lost focus, or a press on something that cannot take focus) does not close it; an outside press is handled by the pointerdown rule. The same rule holds for Menu in the four adapters: React and Vue menus today also close when relatedTarget is null, which changes to the vanilla rule. The listener is on the component's own root, so nothing is attached on the server.

Collapsible: `title: ReactNode` renamed to `label: ReactNode` (required, the content of the summary); the native `title` attribute is no longer omitted from its props.
surface.vue: Popover: `label?: string`, declared without `required: true`; an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute names the panel instead and is moved from the root to the panel. The slot prop `close` and the exposed show() / close() stay. Trigger props: see nav-b-2.

A visible heading is application content: `<h3 id="x">` inside the panel with aria-labelledby="x" on the component.
endState.behaviour: Opening does not move focus; the panel follows the trigger in the tab order. Closing from the content: React through the controlled `open`, Vue through the slot prop close(), Angular through a template reference (`#p`, `p.close(true)`), vanilla through [data-hw-close]. React `disabled`: the trigger is disabled and the popover is closed; an open one closes and notifies false once. Server rendering unchanged: closed unless the open state says otherwise.

conventionConflicts.conflict: The documented vanilla markup nests ul[role=group] inside each tree item; React, Vue and Angular render one flat list with aria-level, aria-posinset and aria-setsize. Rendering the nested markup would mean rewriting selection, focus and click handling in three adapters, because a nested item contains its descendants.
conventionConflicts.closest: The flat list stays (valid ARIA, and the vanilla controller writes the same three attributes). What can be equal is made equal: the toggle button, its class, name and icon, the label span that names the item, and the indentation step (--hw-tree-indent equals the nested step). The flat list has no guide line.

conventionConflicts.conflict: The rule makes data- attributes of the vanilla markup part of the reference DOM. data-hw-trigger, data-hw-panel, data-hw-value, data-hw-close, data-hw-tree-toggle and data-hw-tree-label are hooks that only a vanilla controller reads, and AGENTS.md forbids enhancing a framework tree with vanilla.
conventionConflicts.closest: Frameworks render the elements, hw- classes, roles, ARIA and state attributes (data-variant, data-open) of the reference markup, not the controller hooks. The parity cases select by class and role.

conventionConflicts.conflict: Convention 4 puts an application aria-label before `label`; the kind A mechanism of convention 3 (HwHostAttribute, case ATTR-02) writes `label` while it is given and restores the application's value afterwards, so with both present `label` wins in Angular while the application's aria-label wins in React and Vue (rootLabel).
conventionConflicts.closest: hw-side-navigation follows the mechanism and ATTR-02 as written. The README says to give one source. The cases NAME-01..03 hold in all adapters; only the both-given case differs.
